BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's Draft SPA Positions and Disclosure Letter

The Seller's "FINAL" label and its market commentary (10-20% caps, around 1% baskets, 12-18 month periods) don't bind Wattlebridge. Our playbook governs. We have no record of Amelia Frost approving any of these positions, so we should confirm that with her before we treat any of them as agreed. The Seller's draft departs from the playbook on nearly every material point.

## 1. Departures from the playbook

| Issue | Seller draft | Our playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8M | 25% / AUD 6M starting. 20% is a conditional fallback needing Amelia Frost's written authority, which hasn't been given | Reject. Hold 25%. |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, excess-only (deductible) | AUD 50,000 aggregate, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. Restore a tipping basket at AUD 50k. |
| General claims period (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 needs Amelia Frost's written approval) | Reject. Hold 24 months. |
| Limitation applied to all Claims | Applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise | Separate regimes per category | Reject. Keep general, Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims separate. No general-regime override. |
| Fundamental/Title (capacity, title) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | Reject outright. |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all of these, to the maximum extent enforceable, non-waivable | Reject. Add the fraud carve-out expressly. |
| Disclosure (1.1, 1.2, Schedule 7) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records deemed disclosed | Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room and public-register deemed disclosure | Reject. |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records | Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions | Reject. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry, and must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. |
| Bluefen consent (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of consent; disclosure confirms no final consent yet | Effective consent and evidence that conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Reject. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6M). |
| Riverlark (2/7) | AUD 3.2M outstanding, release "following Completion"; not repaid per disclosure | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases. Post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval | Reject. |
| Employee bonuses (funds flow; disclosure item 5) | AUD 420k excluded from funds flow as "a matter for the Seller"; on-costs unstated | Specific line item or Seller-funded; must not be silently excluded; on-costs must be captured | Reject. Require a specific line item or Seller funding, with on-costs (payroll tax, super) quantified. |
| Ironquay IP (11.1; disclosure item 4) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden the indemnity; preserve the SOW3 cure. AUD 180k is not independently verified either way | Reject "adequate." Broaden the indemnity. Require cure and a confirmatory assignment. Verify the AUD 180k independently. |
| Export/privacy incident DD-006 (4.6; disclosure item 6) | "Preliminary", "not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand either way | Do not accept "not material" as a conclusion. Require log preservation, an investigation timetable and regular updates. Consider a non-numeric specific indemnity (principal sign-off needed). |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | "Ordinary-course operating costs" | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Assess. Do not seek a price deduction on the current record. Test whether each renewal is unavoidable, terminable and accrued, and whether DD-008 and DD-011 overlap. |
| Tax and IP (Seller update) | "Settled under the general regime" | Remain OPEN; no unlimited liability; no resolution | Reject. Keep as open items under their own categories. |
| Title (Seller update; disclosure item 10) | Share register at DD-012 evidences title | DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof | Reject. Require independent title, ownership, encumbrance and authority evidence (ASIC and PPSR searches, Harbourglass authority and approvals, and so on). |

## 2. Reasoning on the most material issues

**Cap, basket and time limit together.** Each Seller term tightens the others. With a AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k excess-only basket, claims up to about AUD 250k in aggregate recover nothing. Combined with a 20% cap and 18 months, this would materially undercut the warranty package. The Seller's "around 1% of price" basket is roughly five times our AUD 50k position and needs to be rejected on the playbook's terms, not argued on market norms.

**Title and fundamentals.** Putting capacity and title under the general cap and time limits is the most serious departure. Title is the core of what we are buying; it should sit outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar with a full cap and at least six years. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale is not a reason to dilute it.

**Fraud carve-out.** The "all Claims of any nature" wording would, on its face, capture fraud and wilful concealment within the limitations and exclusive-remedy provisions. The playbook says no one may waive this. We need an express carve-out, not a general "subject to" qualification.

**Disclosure and knowledge.** Read together, the general disclosure (1.1-1.2) and buyer-knowledge exclusion (8.3) would allow the Seller to disclose everything in the data room and then argue we knew about it. Combined with the reliance and exclusive-remedy provisions, that leaves us with very little recourse. Both need to be deleted or replaced with specific disclosure.

**Bluefen and Riverlark.** The Seller is effectively asking us to take on consent and repayment risk after Completion. The disclosure confirms neither is done. Bluefen supports about 30% of revenue; Riverlark is AUD 3.2M of debt. Both should be conditions or Completion deliverables, not post-Completion promises.

**Stale record.** The data room cut-off is 5.00pm 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. The record needs a bring-down, and the DD-002 to DD-012 items need to be refreshed before we agree anything.

## 3. Open items and limits of this review

- I have only the Seller's summary positions and disclosure letter, not the full marked SPA. Clause references (for example, Bluefen clause 11.3, Ironquay clause 7.3 and the Mossvale and lease provisions) need checking against the full text.
- DD-007 (office lease notification) and DD-009 (Mossvale assignment restriction): the disclosure does not say consent is required for the share sale. We should not assume it is either way; confirm with the Seller and the relevant counterparties.
- The DD-006 export matter and the Sandbar renewals are unresolved facts. The playbook requires us to assume no confirmed breach, harm or payment obligation in either direction.
- Tax and IP positions are open and I have not assessed them against any specific Tax or IP warranty text.

## 4. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the Seller's package as a basis for negotiation.** Do not treat the "FINAL" label or market commentary as binding. Confirm with Amelia Frost whether any principal-level commitments have been made.
2. **General cap:** hold at 25% / AUD 6M. Do not offer 20% unless Amelia Frost gives written authority identifying the draft.
3. **Thresholds:** de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate tipping basket AUD 50,000.
4. **Time limits:** 24 months for general claims. Keep Title/Fundamental separate, at least six years.
5. **Title and fundamentals:** separate regime, 100% cap, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Require independent title evidence, not DD-012 alone.
6. **Fraud:** express carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, non-waivable.
7. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only. Reject data-room, accounts, statutory register and public-register deemed disclosure.
8. **Buyer knowledge:** delete 8.3. Any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry, and never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
9. **Bluefen:** effective consent and evidence of satisfied conditions before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is not enough.
10. **Riverlark:** payout from Completion funds, direct repayment and effective releases at Completion. Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
11. **Employee bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific line item in the funds flow, or Seller-funded.
12. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity beyond SOW3, preserve the cure, require a confirmatory assignment, and independently verify the AUD 180k.
13. **DD-006 export incident:** preserve logs, investigate, require regular updates. Do not accept "not material". Consider a non-numeric specific indemnity, subject to principal sign-off.
14. **Sandbar renewals:** assess only. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
15. **Tax and IP:** keep open, under separate categories, with no unlimited liability and no general-regime override.
16. **Records:** bring down the data room to current date and confirm the status of DD-007 and DD-009 with the Seller.
